question.text: A patient has been diagnosed with advanced Glianorex degeneration, primarily characterized by significant synaptic pruning affecting the Emotoafferen Globuli and the Somatosensory Haptine Threads. This has adversely hit the Glial-Synaptic Density (GSD), preventing the modulated resilience and efficiency of emotional processing. The patient is prone to severe mood swings and struggles with balance. Keeping the Glianorex's nervous system's key components in mind, which of the following would most likely be observed in this patient?

options.A: An upregulation of neurotransmitter Gliotransmitide and Alectorol
options.B: An underactive Sentirex Ganglia and super-sensitive Glioceptors
options.C: A significant decrease in hormones Equilibron and Neurostabilin
options.D: A predisposition to Glianorexic Neuritis, characterized by inflammation of the Psychic Neurexins
options.F: I don't know or cannot answer
